title: Route a Model per Job
tagline: One model per role, each swap a line of configuration an eval can veto.

story.problem: One model served every job, so the question of which model should do which job was never written down anywhere a reviewer could argue with. When it finally got asked, a single sweep over fifteen labelled vendor replies ranked a cheaper model first and the classifier was switched to it — and the very next run of the same fifteen cases scored 11/15 with six schema failures.
story.solution: A per-role registry in agent/lib/models.ts: four roles (planner, scout, classifier, judge), each with a default id, an env override, a context window and a written rationale that the app renders. Resolution runs through one function, and assertKnownModel turns the Token Factory price snapshot into an allowlist so a typo'd id stops the process instead of silently benchmarking a different model.
story.outcome: Two cheap swaps were measured and refused. The classifier stayed on Qwen after probe:schema recorded 0/30 structured-output failures against the cheaper candidate's 4/30, and the scout role was reverted after every specialist session failed with not one vendor recorded against a 46/50 baseline. models:compare now runs three rounds and ranks on the worst one.

prerequisites: A Nebius Token Factory API key as NEBIUS_API_KEY in .env.local
npm install at the repo root
A current price snapshot: npm run pricing:refresh
A labelled dataset for at least one role (evals/data/vendor-replies.json)
